recipes.name: Artichoke Spinach Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can marinated artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed, drained and squeezed dry
1 (4 ounce) package herb and garlic feta, crumbled

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Spray a 9x13 inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add noodles and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.

Spray a large skillet with cooking spray and heat on medium-high. Saute onion and garlic for 3 minutes, or until onion is tender-crisp. Stir in broth and rosemary; bring to a boil. Stir in artichoke hearts and spinach; reduce heat, cover and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in pasta sauce.

Spread 1/4 of the artichoke mixture in the bottom of the prepared baking dish; top with 3 cooked noodles. Sprinkle 3/4 cup mozzarella cheese over noodles. Repeat layers 2 more times, ending with artichoke mixture and mozzarella cheese. Sprinkle crumbled feta on top.
Bake, covered, for 40 minutes. Uncover, and bake 15 minutes more, or until hot and bubbly. Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.

raw_recipe.headline: Artichoke Spinach Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This is a fabulous lasagna made with an artichoke and spinach mixture which has been cooked with vegetable broth, onions and garlic. The mixture is layered with lasagna noodles, pasta sauce, mozzarella cheese, and topped with crumbled feta.

review.reviewBody: I would actually give this a 4.75, only because I found the lasagna to be very watery. Next time I would cut down on the broth. Great tasting, though, and leftovers just as good or better. I used homemade veg broth, which I do for everything. Very easy to make -- just keep all the ends of veggies that you have in a bag in the freezer (carrot ends, broccoli stalks, onion bits, etc). When you have enough to fill a pot, cover them with water and boil until the veggies have basically nothing left! Drain and keep the "broth." You can compost or throw out the soggy veggies, and then freeze the broth for when you need it. Great way to recycle old bits of veggies, and couldn't be healthier or more natural!

Felt this was a promising base recipe to "freestyle" from. It is! Here is my interpretation:

I used sufficient noodles to make three layers in my baking dish. Leave them raw.

Follow directions for preparing the filling as written but add a small can of drained mushroom pieces and stems as the last step. 

Substitute commercial or homemade (always better and super simple to make -- can be done the day before) VODKA sauce for called for traditional red sauce. 

Assemble as directed but add 1/2-1 c. of water/broth around the edges of the lasagna before covering with tightly sealed foil. Finally, skip the feta.

The result is a beautifully balanced dance of flavors working together to produce a complex sophisticated flavor where each ingredient can be tasted but no one ingredient overwhelms.

Serve with chilled Pinot Grigio and crusty garlic bread. A meal fit for company or a hungry family!

Easy and delicious. The marinated artichokes were key! The store didn't have herb and garlic feta so we used plain and it was still great! We used oven ready noodles. We did not find it too runny at all - I think squeezing the spinach, letting it sit for a min and then squeeze the spinach again in a paper towel really reduced the potential liquid in the dish. It's not a photogenic dish, but we'll make it regularly!

Very flavorful. I increased the mozzarella to 4 cups. I used a big and small size jar of the artichokes and used fresh baby spinach that I cooked up in a little butter and then pressed out as much moisture as possible.

UPDATE: After making this Lasagna umpteen times I decided to use Frozen Chopped Collards Greens because they're my Favs, and they tastes great too! This Artichoke-Spinach Lasagna is fabulous "as is" (per the recipe) but I added 16 ounces of White Button Mushrooms (stems removed, then cleaned and sliced) for flavor and texture. This is THE BEST Lasagna I've ever made and I've making/baking Lasagna for 20+ years!!

This recipe is amazing. I think as others mentioned in their reviews, a white Alfredo sauce would pair perfectly however it is great with red sauce too. I also used the regular uncooked lasagna noodles that were suggested in the reviews and I like the tall lasagna so I used a smaller square baking dish. Substituted the basil for the rosemary and used fresh spinach instead of frozen. This definitely is a keeper. Love it!!!
followed someone's recommendation of using only 1 cup of broth, and I scooped the filling from the pan to not add excess liquid update: way better with fresh spinach and added mushrooms!

This is delicious. Coming from a person who doesn’t usually like veggie lasagna. I did use fresh spinach instead of frozen and tomato purée instead of pasta sauce. I also didn’t pre cook the noodles. I made sure they were all covered in sauce and they have the perfect bite to them. It was a lot more hearty and substantial that I thought it’d be!l

Everyone absolutely loved it. I followed directions except that I used fresh spinach instead of frozen. About 10 ounces I guess. I didn’t quite dice it…but smaller than a chop. Also, I cooked it 40 minutes covered, 25 uncovered(10 more than in directions because it seemed wet), and then let it sit for about 20. Also, I couldn’t find Garlic & herb feta so I used Garlic & tomato feta. I also used 4 Cups Mozz instead of 3. Don’t pay attention to the comments about it being too wet. Also used no boil Gluten Free lasagna noodles. If you didn’t tell people there was no meat in here they wouldn’t even know.

Okay, this recipe is a winner. We have vegetarian friends, so I’m always looking for ways to satisfy all of us without compromising their dietary lifestyle.

The recipe was fun to make. It went together faster than my usual lasagna, and was far more nutritious.

I took hints from previous reviewers. The layer of ricotta, Italian seasoning, and basil added an extra dimension we all enjoyed. The use of fewer lasagna noodles added to the flavor as well. (Next time I’ll substitute thin-sliced eggplant.)

This recipe is a keeper. Thanks so much for sharing it with us.

Pretty dang delish. Made my own "herb and garlic feta", added a pound of Italian sausage. Increased mozzarella, and decreased noodles by 1/3. Recommend not overcooking the onions, as the crispness gave the dish a whole new texture which was awesome. Boyfriend loved this dish! (And that's impressive, because he is definitely a better cook than I am.)
A keeper!

Pretty impressively had every family member getting seconds. I'll use maybe half the amount of broth next time (but no-boil noodles would work better with this amount). One of the kids "hates" artichokes but loved it unsuspectingly, saying it tasted like gourmet deep dish pizza. The artichokes are the star, bringing a wonderful tang, better and less intense than olives. I used a pound of fresh spinach, steamed, squeezed thoroughly, and chopped fine.
Loved it!
Great recipe. Used fresh spinach and added a few mushrooms. Everyone loved it.

This has been my favorite vegetarian lasagna recipes for YEARS. I’ve always simply used uncooked noodles to soak up all of the extra liquid. I also don’t bother draining the spinach. Try it. It makes this recipe perfect!

I followed this recipe exactly and did not love it. I felt the rosemary and feta were too overpowering, and I didn't like the combination of spinach/artichoke with tomato sauce. I tried it again substituting the feta with mozzarella and parmesan, and used a homemade light alfredo sauce instead of tomato sauce. It was outstanding and I've made it a few times with these tweaks, including adding a cup of cooked chicken breast in the middle layer. I know this is a big difference from the original recipe, but I liked it much better with these substitutions.
Very tasty

I added six sliced baby Bella mushrooms, sautéed with the onions, also substituted chicken broth for the vegetable broth. I didn’t have fresh rosemary so I added 1/2 tsp dried. This recipe is Delicious! Thank you
I left out the rosemary and feta - due to allergy and dislike of feta. Still delicious. I prefer this over traditional lasagna.
